questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving Exponential Functions with the Same Exponents and a Polynomial
questions.worked_solution:
First, we move all the terms to the left side of the inequality and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x{e}^{5x}-3{e}^{5x} & \ge -{x}^{2}{e}^{5x} \\ {x}^{2}{e}^{5x}-2x{e}^{5x}-3{e}^{5x} & \ge 0 \\ ({x}^{2}-2x-3){e}^{5x} & \ge 0 \\ (x+1)(x-3){e}^{5x} & \ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we divide both sides by ${e}^{5x}$ and get

$$
(x+1)(x-3)\ge 0.
$$

This represents an upwards parabola whose roots are at $x=-1$ and $x=3.$ The parabola is above the $x$-axis when $x\le -1$ or $x\ge 3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14036850/assets/6aca0f7c055a5f326c2d0d3bc65b6e68a90c8cb496bc1934dbae6093d0d71f96.png)

Therefore, the solution is $x\le -1$ or $x\ge 3.$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we move all the terms to the left side of the inequality and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{9}^{2x-4}{x}^{2} & <-5\cdot {9}^{2x-4}-7\cdot {9}^{2x-4} \\ -{9}^{2x-4}{x}^{2}+5\cdot {9}^{2x-4}+7\cdot {9}^{2x-4} & <0 \\ (-{x}^{2}+5+7){9}^{2x-4} & <0 \\ (12-{x}^{2}){9}^{2x-4} & <0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we divide both sides by ${9}^{2x-4}$ and solve the resulting inequality using familiar techniques:

$$
\begin{aligned}12-{x}^{2} & <0 \\ -{x}^{2} & <-12 \\ {x}^{2} & >12 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & >\sqrt{12} \\ |x| & >2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to the inequality above is $x<-2\sqrt{3}$ or $x>2\sqrt{3}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving Exponential Functions with Different Exponents and a Polynomial
questions.worked_solution:
First, we move all the terms to the left side of the inequality and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot {9}^{2x-3} & \le {9}^{2x+1} \\ {x}^{2}\cdot {9}^{2x-3}-{9}^{2x+1} & \le 0 \\ {x}^{2}\cdot {9}^{2x-3}-{9}^{4}\cdot {9}^{2x-3} & \le 0 \\ ({x}^{2}-{9}^{4})\cdot {9}^{2x-3} & \le 0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we divide both sides by ${9}^{2x-3}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{({x}^{2}-{9}^{4})\cdot {9}^{2x-3}}{{9}^{2x-3}} & \le \frac{0}{{9}^{2x-3}} \\ {x}^{2}-{9}^{4} & \le 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve this inequality using familiar methods:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{9}^{4} & \le 0 \\ {x}^{2} & \le {9}^{4} \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & \le \sqrt{{9}^{4}} \\ |x| & \le {9}^{2} \\ |x| & \le 81\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to the inequality above is $-81\le x<81.$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we move all the terms to the left side of the inequality and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}\cdot {4}^{3x-5} & \ge {4}^{3x-1} \\ {x}^{4}\cdot {4}^{3x-5}-{4}^{3x-1} & \ge 0 \\ {x}^{4}\cdot {4}^{3x-5}-{4}^{4}\cdot {4}^{3x-5} & \ge 0 \\ ({x}^{4}-{4}^{4}){4}^{3x-5} & \ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we divide both sides by ${4}^{3x-5}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{({x}^{4}-{4}^{4}){4}^{3x-5}}{{4}^{3x-5}} & \ge \frac{0}{{4}^{3x-5}} \\ {x}^{4}-{4}^{4} & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve this inequality using familiar methods:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{4}^{4} & \ge 0 \\ {x}^{4} & \ge {4}^{4} \\ \sqrt[4]{{x}^{4}} & \ge \sqrt[4]{{4}^{4}} \\ |x| & \ge 4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the inequality above is  $x\le -4$ or $x\ge 4.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot {3}^{2x-5} & \ge {3}^{2x-3} \\ {x}^{2}\cdot {3}^{2x-5}-{3}^{2x-3} & \ge 0 \\ {x}^{2}\cdot {3}^{2x-5}-{3}^{2}\cdot {3}^{2x-5} & \ge 0 \\ ({x}^{2}-{3}^{2}){3}^{2x-5} & \ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we divide both sides by ${3}^{2x-5}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{({x}^{2}-{3}^{2}){2}^{2x-5}}{{3}^{2x-5}} & \ge \frac{0}{{3}^{2x-5}} \\ {x}^{2}-{3}^{2} & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve this inequality using familiar methods:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{3}^{2} & \ge 0 \\ {x}^{2} & \ge {3}^{2} \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & \ge \sqrt{{3}^{2}} \\ |x| & \ge 3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the inequality above is  $x\le -3$ or $x\ge 3.$
